provenance.l: Beagle 2 ESA/UK Commission of Inquiry report (5 April 2004) §3: entry at 5.5 km/s; Mach 1 in under 3 min, pilot chute; front shield and back cover released, main chute; altimeter; air-bags inflated at 200 m; rebounds up to 28 m (risk of bouncing into the main parachute). Entry angle, chute size and the shield/cover mass split are not given — estimated
NASA — Beagle 2 in depth: 69 kg at launch, 33.2 kg lander at touchdown; landed 25 Dec 2003, found partly deployed by MRO in 2015

Beagle 2 EDL as researched for pass 2 (2026-11-23, docs/wip/2026-11-23-mars-landings-record.md): aeroshell 0.93 m, lander 0.66 m; pilot chute 1.9 m, then a 10 m main at about 2.6 km (the Cd·A of 43 m² is a 0.55 disc-gap-band over the 10 m disc, an estimate); three gas bags inflated at about 280 m (the inquiry report above says 200 m), each segment 1.93 x 0.965 m; the main chute is released at first impact, with no bridle cut; the lander dropped about 1 m when the bags were released; four 0.57 m pentagonal panels, of which HiRISE shows 3, possibly 4, deployed (the mission failed: drawn as 3 open and the last one not). Back cover 11.8 kg is 69 − 33.2 − 24 (the shield split is an estimate); the bounce count, roll and time to rest are drawn, not sourced; the first rebound is the inquiry report’s 28 m
ESA — Beagle 2 lander found on Mars (HiRISE, 2015): partly deployed, one panel blocking the antenna
